kept.heading: AI FEARS ARE FUELING THE ‘HANDMADE' BRANDING TREND (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Brands across industries are using handmade aesthetics to signal humanity in an AI-saturated market. Think hand-drawn typography, imperfect textures, retro illustrations, and intentionally ‘rough' design. The trend is showing up in food, cleaning products, luxury hospitality, and even AI brands like Claude. However, when brands use these cues without meaning, they can feel generic and fail to stand out. Handmade elements work best when they fit the brand or concept.

kept.heading: GOOGLE LOWERS SEARCH PROFILE REQUIREMENTS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google lowered the follower threshold for its Search profiles, making the feature available to more brands and creators. YouTube, Instagram, and X accounts now qualify at 35K followers or subscribers, down from 100K. TikTok's threshold dropped from 300K to 100K. Google also added new Search Console reporting on search terms, rankings, and search volume. On YouTube, channel managers will now receive alerts for copyright claims and removal requests, giving teams more visibility into issues that could affect content.

kept.heading: OOPS! SORRY FOR THE MISTAKE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Use a believable “mistake” to earn a second email. Send an initial email with something intentionally wrong (ie. a broken link, placeholder text, or early promotion). Follow up minutes later with an “oops” apology and the real offer. The first email creates curiosity and gets attention. The follow-up feels more human and gives you a natural place to add a discount or incentive. Use this sparingly, as repeating this tactic too often makes it obvious.

kept.heading: HOW SHOWING A TEAM MEMBER INCREASED LEADS BY 79% (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Showing the person behind a service can make a landing page more persuasive when customers need reassurance before taking action. For a financial services client, replacing a calculator-focused headline with “Is equity release right for me?” and introducing a real information team member increased completed leads by 79%. The test worked by bringing the team's reputation for empathy and clear guidance onto the page before visitors had to contact them. Identify persuasive assets that already exist in the business and surface them where prospects need reassurance.

kept.heading: WRITING FOR HUMANS: THE REAL AI WORKFLOWS BEHIND GREAT B2B CONTENT (WEBINAR)
kept.blurb: Join this webinar on August 21 at 12 PM EST for a 1-hour session on using AI to create high-quality B2B content. Speakers, including Amanda Natividad of SparkToro, Jenny Coppola of Bitly, and Meghan Crook Brisson of Intentsify, will share their workflows. They'll cover the tools and prompts they use, what they write themselves, and how they evaluate AI output.

kept.heading: AN UPDATE TO HOW WE COUNT PUBLIC VIEWS ACROSS YOUTUBE (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: YouTube will change how it counts public views across all video formats starting on August 24. A view will count as soon as a video begins playing, including the first frame, which will likely increase reported view counts. YouTube will keep “Engaged views” in Analytics to show how many viewers continued watching. The change won't affect creator earnings or YouTube Partner Program eligibility, which will continue to use engaged or qualified views and watch hours.

kept.heading: HOW AI TEXT WATERMARKING WORKS (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Claude's text watermarking will be difficult to remove without heavy edits. Instead of visible characters, AI watermarks hide in word choices, using secret statistical patterns that can survive copying. Detection requires the provider's secret key and enough text to distinguish the watermark from chance, making it different from style-based AI detectors. Light editing or paraphrasing can weaken the signal but may leave enough original wording to remain detectable.

kept.heading: CONTENT EFFORT: THE GOOGLE RANKING FEATURE NOBODY TALKS ABOUT (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Google defines content effort as the extent to which a human actively worked to create satisfying content. In practice, that means showing evidence of unique value through original research and firsthand insights, rather than recycled facts or AI-generated summaries. Organize content around the user's goal, put the most useful information upfront, and cut filler. AI can help with production, but scaled content that adds little beyond what already exists is unlikely to stand out. Before publishing, ask whether the page contains something competitors can't easily reproduce.

kept.heading: 37 PROVEN WAYS TO USE AI IN MARKETING (28 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Useful ways to use AI for SEO, content, analysis, and more.

kept.heading: WHAT 9 MONTHS OF AI OVERVIEW DATA AND 51,000+ TRACKED EVENTS REVEAL (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: AI Overviews are becoming a meaningful but highly volatile source of organic traffic. In nine months of data, AI Overviews accounted for 7.53% of organic sessions, yet 22.4% of those events were misattributed to Direct. Google also favored specific, structured content such as pricing, travel times, routes, and HTML comparison tables, while stale content lost citation share over time. Surface the #:~:text= signal in GA4 to track AIO traffic directly rather than relying on standard GA4 reporting. Additionally, use citation data to prioritize content updates and avoid treating any single AI Overview traffic level as a stable baseline.

kept.heading: WHY PLATFORMS ARE GETTING WEIRDER TO GROW WIDER (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Growth is flatlining for social platforms, so they are blurring the line between social feeds, streaming, and connected TV to find new reach. TikTok now exports creator videos built on Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars IP straight into the Disney+ app, giving entertainment and licensing brands an IP-cleared path to top-of-funnel audiences. Pinterest is testing whether a shoppable home-makeover show on Roku, packed with QR codes to buyable boards, can turn passive TV viewing into direct sales.

kept.heading: INSIDE BETTERHELP'S ‘REPEATABLE, SCALABLE' COMMENTS-SECTION SOCIAL STRATEGY (4 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: BetterHelp's growth team stumbled into a strategy after one TikTok comment pulled in more than 300,000 likes. That single moment turned into a deliberate program. The brand now comments on 200 to 350 posts a month, with 10 to 20 of those regularly crossing 10,000 likes. Daily new followers have grown roughly a hundredfold since the team committed to the approach last fall. The rule that makes it work is narrow - only join conversations where a mental-health brand has an obvious, earned reason to speak, and never pitch a sale in the comments themselves.

kept.heading: MARKETING EXPERIMENTATION FRAMEWORK: HOW TO RUN BETTER TESTS (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Use the CLEAR framework to prioritize experiments based on commercial opportunity, learning value, evidence strength, addressability, and resource requirements, then define the decision each possible outcome will trigger before the test begins. Set commercial success thresholds alongside statistical criteria so a measurable result only leads to action when it creates enough value to justify implementation. Feed proven learnings into future planning so teams stop retesting known questions and focus resources on the smaller set of uncertainties that can materially improve marketing performance.

kept.heading: HOW TO AUDIT YOUR LINKEDIN CONVERSION TRACKING SETUP (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Don't treat LinkedIn Conversions API as set-and-forget. Audit the setup regularly across three areas. First, confirm the CRM consistently captures key funnel events and that fields and workflows are up to date. Then compare LinkedIn's conversion data with the CRM to catch missing, misnamed, or incorrectly attributed events. Finally, assign a clear owner and document the setup so changes to the marketing stack don't break tracking. Fix CRM gaps first, then data mapping issues, and establish an ongoing review process to keep reporting reliable.

kept.heading: REDDIT IS TESTING AUDIO AND VIDEO VERSIONS OF POPULAR POSTS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Reddit is testing audio and video versions of its most popular posts, letting users choose to read or play a thread inside its iOS and Android apps. The test stays limited to select English-language communities and does not replace the original text or comments. Creators already turn viral Reddit posts into podcast-style content on TikTok, Reels, and YouTube Shorts, often narrating them over unrelated footage. Reddit does not own that experience yet, and this test is an attempt to bring it back in-house.

kept.heading: NARRATIVE DEBT (6 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: “Narrative debt” is the tension created when content raises a question, makes a promise, or opens a loop. The bigger the promise, the longer people will wait for the payoff. Small questions should be answered quickly, while larger ones can unfold over time. Avoid opening too many loops at once, which can make content feel scattered. Instead, keep a few strong questions open and pay them off at the right moments to maintain attention.

kept.heading: WHERE THE BETTER-FOR-YOU AISLE GROWS NEXT (14 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: A study of 100 better-for-you drink buyers found a major retention problem, with 35% no longer regularly buying any of the five brands studied. Retention was stronger when a drink replaced something specific, like soda, rather than water or nothing. OLIPOP retained 65% of buyers who used it instead of soda, compared with 25% who replaced nothing. Liquid Death could similarly position itself as an alternative to beer in social settings. Brands should focus on the specific habit they're replacing while addressing barriers like packaging and distribution.

kept.heading: 265 MILLION PEOPLE STILL LOVE CANVA. THE MARKET TOOK $11 BILLION OFF ANYWAY (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Canva has 265M monthly users, but AI is changing how those users interact with the product. AI agents can now create designs without sending users to Canva, potentially bypassing the platform entirely. At the same time, AI assistants are recommending Canva, with users having 26M+ conversations with its ChatGPT app. The shift creates a new challenge for brands. AI can both send customers to a product and remove the need for it.

kept.heading: AMERICANS AREN'T SOLD ON BUSINESSES USING AI IN ADVERTISING (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Consumers aren't rejecting AI in advertising outright - they're drawing a sharp line at whose face and voice ends up in the ad. Most Americans accept AI for brainstorming and drafting, and just over half are fine with AI producing the final ad content itself. However, nearly two in three say using AI to create a person's likeness or voice crosses a line, even when a business discloses it. Young adults under 30 are the least forgiving group by far, with 66% viewing AI-made advertising negatively overall and 73% rejecting AI-generated people or voices specifically.

kept.heading: WIN REPORT: WHY ADDING AN EXTRA STEP TO A FUNNEL INCREASED ORDER VALUE BY 28% (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Moving an upsell to its own step can increase order value without hurting conversion when it removes competing decisions from the main purchase page. A South American gift company moved add-ons from the bottom of its product pages to an interstitial page after customers selected a gift. The change increased revenue-per-order by 28% and had no impact on overall conversion. The test shows that funnel friction depends on context, and giving secondary offers their own moment can make them more visible without making the purchase harder.

kept.heading: CHATGPT DEFAULTS TO BRANDED SEARCH FOR "X BEST SOFTWARE" QUERIES (3 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: ChatGPT often starts product searches from a preselected set of brands it already associates with a category, making category eligibility more important than traditional SEO rankings. In one example, its first search for enterprise AI agent platforms already included Microsoft, Salesforce, Google, ServiceNow, IBM, and AWS before any neutral market scan. Challenger brands need repeated category association through owned content, comparison pages, third-party validation, analyst coverage, customer proof, and clear product messaging to enter these default vendor sets. Research suggests that appearing in ChatGPT's generated search query can be worth about 33 times more than simply being discoverable.

kept.heading: AI TRANSPARENCY & DISCLOSURE FRAMEWORK V2 (1 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: The IAB's updated framework gives brands, agencies, publishers, and technology partners practical triggers for disclosing AI-generated or AI-assisted text, images, video, audio, synthetic voices, digital twins, and consumer interactions. It also aims to prevent disclosure fatigue by avoiding labels when AI use is not materially relevant to the consumer experience.

kept.heading: OPENAI LAUNCHES A SAFER CHATGPT FOR TEENS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: ChatGPT for Teens has added safety measures and tools designed to reduce AI-assisted cheating. The experience includes Study Mode, which guides students through problems instead of giving quick answers, plus quizzes, learning visualizations, homework reminders, and parental controls. OpenAI is also adding age-appropriate content protections and partnering with CodeAI to teach teens how to use and question AI.

kept.heading: STOP MAKING THE CREATOR THE HERO: A TALENT AGENCY FOUNDER'S HYPE CHECK (51 MINUTE PODCAST)
kept.blurb: Mega-influencers and celebrities still drive results, but brands often use them incorrectly. This podcast breaks down how to negotiate celebrity rates, when to use top-of-funnel versus bottom-of-funnel creators, and how whitelisting can turn creator content into a performance channel. It also covers why long-term creator partnerships aren't always the best approach and how brands can land major talent without paying traditional talent fees.

kept.heading: WHY TYLER SPEEGLE TREATS HIS CREATOR BUSINESS LIKE A MARKETER WOULD (5 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Creator Tyler Speegle uses his marketing background to treat content like an A/B test, analyzing what drives views and iterating on it. He also turned repeated audience questions about his homemade seasonings into his own product line. The move gave him a new revenue stream while creating conflicts with competing sponsorships. He now uses content to drive product launches, including seasonal releases and a planned cookbook.

kept.heading: ANTHROPIC'S TEXT WATERMARKING PROVES AI COMPANIES DO NOT CARE AT ALL ABOUT WRITING (7 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Anthropic's new watermarking works by quietly changing which word Claude picks when two options seem equally good. It swaps in a hidden key instead of plain randomness, so the pattern stays invisible to readers but detectable later. The company treats that kind of choice as low stakes, the difference between grey and overcast. However, word choice for a human writer usually carries intent, mood, and context that a statistical model can't see. Anthropic says internal testing found no measurable drop in quality or creativity from the change. The bigger problem isn't the watermark itself. It's that a company building writing tools thinks words are interchangeable in the first place.

kept.heading: TIKTOK LIVE ADDS AI-GENERATED INTROS (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: TikTok launched an AI tool in its LIVE composer that generates shareable summaries of hosts and their broadcasts.

kept.heading: HAS APPLE DROPPED THE BALL WITH ITS GEN Z MARKETING? (2 MINUTE READ)
kept.blurb: Apple's new TikTok-first, meme-heavy marketing pleases the TikTok crowd but is drawing backlash from longtime fans who want the classic, understated Apple back.
